Hydraulic redistribution is a passive mechanism where water is transported from moist to dry soils via subterranean networks.

Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Hypnagogia is the transitional state from [wakefulness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wakefulness) to [sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep), also defined as the waning state of [consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consciousness) during the [onset of sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onset_of_sleep).

Hypnopompia (also known as hypnopompic state) is the [state of consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_consciousness) leading out of [sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep), a term coined by the [psychical researcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychical_researcher) [Frederic Myers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederic_William_Henry_Myers).

hyponastic response is a [nastic movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nastic_movement) characterized by an upward bending of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) or other [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) parts, resulting from accelerated growth of the lower side of the [petiole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petiole_(botany)) in comparison to its upper part.

Hypoventilation training is a physical training method in which periods of exercise with reduced [breathing frequency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breathing_frequency) are interspersed with periods with normal [breathing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breathing).
Hypoxemia (also spelled hypoxaemia) is an abnormally low level of [oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen) in the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood).

Hysterical strength is a display of extreme [physical strength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_strength) by humans, beyond what is believed to be within their capacity, usually occurring when people are in—or perceive themselves, or others, to be in—[life-or-death situations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight-or-flight_response).

definition: inflammatory reflex is a neural circuit that regulates the [immune response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_response) to [injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury) and invasion.

Injury is [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) damage to the living tissue of any organism, whether [in humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury_in_humans), [in other animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury_in_animals), or [in plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury_in_plants).
Injury in plants is damage caused by other organisms or by the non-living (abiotic) environment to plants.

Insect olfaction refers to the function of [chemical receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_receptor)s that enable [insects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insects) to detect and identify [volatile compounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volatile_organic_compound) for [foraging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foraging), predator avoidance, finding [mating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating) partners (via [pheromone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheromone)s) and locating [oviposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oviposition) habitats.

Insect olfactory receptors (also known as odorant receptors, ORs) are expressed in the [cell membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membranes) of the olfactory sensory neurons of [insects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insects).
Insect thermoregulation is the process whereby insects maintain body temperatures within certain boundaries.

Insect winter ecology describes the [overwinter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overwinter) survival strategies of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, which are in many respects more similar to those of plants than to many other animals, such as mammals and birds.

instinctive drowning response is an [instinctive reaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instinct) that occurs in humans, particularly in non-swimmers, when close to [drowning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowning).
insulin index of food represents how much it elevates the concentration of [insulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insulin) in the blood during the two-hour period after the food is ingested.

Integrative neuroscience is the study of [neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroscience) that works to unify functional organization data to better understand complex structures and behaviors.
Inter-ictal spiking refers to abnormal neuronal discharges between [epileptic seizure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epileptic_seizure)s.

Intermuscular Coherence is a measure to quantify correlations between the activity of two [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s, which is often assessed using [electromyography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromyography).

internal environment (or milieu intérieur in [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language); ) was a concept developed by [Claude Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Bernard), and he received a [Nobel Prize in chemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Chemistry) in 1992 for this contribution to the theory of electron transfer reactions in chemical systems.
International Union of Physiological Sciences, abbreviated IUPS, is the global umbrella organization for [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).
Interoception is the collection of [[Sense#Other internal sensations and perceptions|senses]] providing information to the organism about the internal state of the body.

Intracranial pressure (ICP) is the pressure exerted by fluids such as [cerebrospinal fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrospinal_fluid) (CSF) inside the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) and on the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) tissue.
intrapleural pressure is the pressure within the [pleural cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleural_cavity).

Intrinsic ageing and extrinsic ageing are terms used to describe [cutaneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutaneous) ageing of the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) and other parts of the [integumentary system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integumentary_system), which while having [epidermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) [[wikt: concomitant|concomitants]], seems to primarily involve the [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis).
Irritability is the excitatory ability that [living organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_organisms) have to respond to changes in their environment.

Irritation, in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), is a state of [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) or painful reaction to [allergy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allergy) or cell-lining damage.
isometric exercise is an exercise involving the static contraction of a muscle without any visible movement in the angle of the joint.

isometric contraction is an event occurring in early [systole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systole_(medicine)) during which the [ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)) contract with no corresponding [volume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume) change ([[wikt:isometric#Adjective|isometrically]]).

Isovolumic relaxation time (IVRT) is an interval in the [cardiac cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_cycle), from the aortic component of the second [heart sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_sound), that is, closure of the [aortic valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aortic_valve), to onset of filling by opening of the mitral valve.

Kinesiology () is the scientific study of [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) movement.

Phosphorus deficiency is a plant disorder associated with insufficient supply of phosphorus.
Photoperiod is the change of [day length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daylight) over the [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season)s.
photophobia (adjective: photophobic) is negative response to light.
Photoprotection is the biochemical process that helps organisms cope with molecular damage caused by [sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight).
photosensitivity is an abnormal reaction of the skin to light.

Photosynthesis ( ) The salvaging pathway for the products of RuBisCO oxygenase activity is more commonly known as photorespiration, since it is characterized by light-dependent oxygen consumption and the release of carbon dioxide.

Photosynthesis systems are [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronics) [scientific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific) instruments designed for non-destructive measurement of [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) rates in the field.

physical activity level (PAL) is a way to express a person's daily [physical activity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_activity) as a number and is used to estimate their [energy expenditure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_expenditure).
Physical literacy is the ability to move with competence and confidence in a wide variety of physical activities in multiple environments that benefit the healthy development of the whole person.

Physiologia Plantarum is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) on behalf of the [Scandinavian Plant Physiology Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scandinavian_Plant_Physiology_Society).

Physiological condition is a term used in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology), [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), and [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine).
Physiological functional capacity (PFC) is the ability to perform the physical tasks of [daily life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daily_life) and the ease with which these tasks can be performed.

Physiological plant disorders are caused by non-[pathological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathological) conditions such as poor light, adverse weather, water-logging, [phytotoxic compounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytotoxicity) or a lack of nutrients, and affect the functioning of the [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) system.

definition: physiological prematurity (also described as [altriciality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altriciality)) refers to the fact that compared to most animals, humans are born in a premature biological state.

Physiological psychology is a subdivision of [behavioral neuroscience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioral_neuroscience) (biological psychology) that studies the neural mechanisms of [perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perception) and behavior through direct manipulation of the brains of nonhuman animal subjects in [controlled experiments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_control).

Physiological Reports is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [open access](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_access) [online](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_and_offline)-only [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) covering original research in all areas of [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology).
Physiological Reviews is a journal published quarterly by the [American Physiological Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Physiological_Society) which has been published since 1921.

physiology of decompression is the aspect of physiology which is affected by exposure to large changes in [ambient pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambient_pressure).

physiology of underwater diving is the physiological adaptations to diving of air-breathing [vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) that have returned to the ocean from terrestrial lineages.
physiome of an individual's or [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species)' [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) state is the description of its functional behavior.

pineal gland (also called the pineal body) is a small [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland) in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) of most [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

Pith, or medulla, is a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s of [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.

planidium is a specialized form of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) seen in the first-[instar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instar) of a few families of insects that have [parasitoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitoid)al ways of life.
Plant bioacoustics refers to the creation of sound waves by plants.

plant cuticle is a protecting film covering the outermost skin layer ([epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany))) of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), young shoots and other aerial plant organs (aerial here meaning all plant parts not embedded in soil or other substrate) that have no [[Bark (botany)#Periderm|periderm]].

Plant defense against herbivory or host-plant resistance is a range of [adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation)s [evolved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution) by [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants) which improve their [survival and reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitness_(biology)) by reducing the impact of [herbivore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivore)s.

Plant growth analysis refers to a set of concepts and equations by which changes in size of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s over time can be summarised and dissected in component variables.
Plant nucleus movement is the movement of the [cell nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) in plants by the [cytoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoskeleton).

Plant perception is the ability of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s to sense and respond to the environment by adjusting their [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_morphology) and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_physiology).

Plant physiology is a subdiscipline of [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany) concerned with the functioning, or [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology), of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Plant Physiology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) scientific journal covering research in [plant physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_physiology), [biochemistry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biochemistry), [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology), [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), [genetics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics), [biophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biophysics), and [environmental biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_biology) of plants.

Plant Proteome Database is a [National Science Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Science_Foundation)-funded project to determine the biological function of each [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.
Plant root exudates are fluids emitted through the roots of plants.
Plant [senescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senescence) is the process of aging in plants.
Plant stress measurement is the [quantification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quantification_(science)) of environmental effects on plant health.

Plasmolysis is the process in which cells lose water in a [hypertonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertonic) solution.

plastid is a [membrane-bound organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane-bound_organelle) found in the [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s of [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants), [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae), and some other [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) organisms.

plithotaxis () is the tendency for each individual [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) within a [monolayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monolayer) to [migrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_migration) along the local orientation of the maximal [principal stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_stress), or equivalently, minimal intercellular [shear stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shear_stress).

definition: pneumatodes are air-containing structures in plant roots.

Poikilohydry is the lack of ability (structural or functional mechanism) to maintain and/or regulate water content to achieve [homeostasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeostasis) of cells and tissue connected with quick equilibration of cell/tissue water content to that of the environment.
poikilotherm () is an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) (Greek poikilos – 'various', 'spotted', and therme – 'heat') whose internal temperature varies considerably.
pollen tube is a tubular structure produced by the male [gametophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gametophyte) of [seed plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_plants) when it germinates.
Polyembryony is the phenomenon of two or more [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)s developing from a single fertilized egg.

population spike (PS) is the shift in electrical potential as a consequence of the movement of ions involved in the generation and propagation of [action potentials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potentials).
postictal state is the [altered state of consciousness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Altered_state_of_consciousness) after an [epileptic seizure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epileptic_seizure).

Postprandial somnolence (colloquially known as food coma or after-meal dip) is a benign state of [drowsiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drowsiness) or [lassitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lassitude) following a meal, a general state of sleepiness and low energy related to activation of the [parasympathetic nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasympathetic_nervous_system) in response to mass in the [gastrointestinal tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_tract).

potometer (from Greek ποτό = drunken, and μέτρο = measure), sometimes known as transpirometer, is a device used for measuring the rate of [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) uptake of a [leaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf)y [shoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoot_(botany)) which is almost equal to the water lost through transpiration.

preBötzinger complex, often abbreviated as preBötC, is a functionally and anatomically specialized site in the ventral-lateral region of the lower [medulla oblongata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medulla_oblongata) (i.e., lower [brainstem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainstem)).

Precordial concordance, also known as QRS concordance, is a pattern in which all [precordial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precordial) [[Electrocardiography#Electrodes and leads|leads]] on an [electrocardiogram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrocardiogram) are either positive (positive concordance: all the [major spikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QRS_complex) point upwards from the baseline) or negative (negative concordance: point downwards).

Preferential motor reinnervation (PMR) refers to the tendency of a [regenerating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroregeneration) [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon) in the [peripheral nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peripheral_nervous_system) (PNS) to [reinnervate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinnervate) a motor pathway as opposed to a [somatosensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somatosensory) pathway.

Preflexes are the latent capacities in the [musculoskeletal system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musculoskeletal_system) that auto-stabilize movements through the use of the [nonlinear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonlinear_system) [visco-elastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscoelasticity) properties of [muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_muscle) when they [contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle_contraction).
Pregnancy has been traditionally defined as the period of time eggs are incubated in the body after the egg-sperm union.

preload is the amount of [sarcomere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcomere) stretch experienced by [cardiac muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle) cells, called [cardiomyocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle_cell), at the end of ventricular filling during [diastole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diastole).
Premovement neuronal activity in neurophysiological literature refers to neuronal modulations that alter the rate at which neurons fire before a subject produces movement.
Preoperational anxiety, or preoperative anxiety, is a common reaction experienced by patients who are admitted to a hospital for [surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgery).

Pressure overload of the right ventricle leads to [right ventricular hypertrophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_ventricular_hypertrophy); right image.]] Pressure overload refers to the pathological state of [cardiac muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle) in which it has to contract while experiencing an excessive [afterload](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afterload).

Pressure reactivity index or PRx is a tool for monitoring cerebral autoregulation in the [intensive care](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensive_care) setting for patients with severe [traumatic brain injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traumatic_brain_injury) or [subarachnoid haemorrhage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subarachnoid_haemorrhage), in order to guide therapy to protect the brain from dangerously high or low [cerebral blood flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_blood_flow).

Primary nutritional groups are groups of [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s, divided according to the sources of energy, electrons, and carbon needed for living, growth, and reproduction.

Pro-oxidants are chemicals that induce [oxidative stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidative_stress), either by generating [reactive oxygen species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reactive_oxygen_species) or by inhibiting [antioxidant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioxidant) systems.

Professorship of Physiology, also known as the Chair of Physiology (1883), is a [chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_(highest_academic_rank)) at the [University of Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Cambridge).

The law of the prolonged [sine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sine) was observed when measuring the strength of the reaction of the plant stems and roots in response to turning from their usual vertical orientation.

proteolipid is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) covalently linked to [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid) molecules, which can be [fatty acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatty_acid)s, [isoprenoids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terpenoid) or [sterol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterol)s.

Protoplast (), is a [biological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) term coined by [Hanstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_von_Hanstein) in 1880 to refer to the entire cell, excluding the cell wall.
Pseudo-response regulator (PRR) refers to a group of genes that regulate the [circadian oscillator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_oscillator) in plants.
Psychology, philosophy and physiology (PPP) was a [degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_degree) program at the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford).

Psychophysiological economics is a field of study focused on the assessment and evaluation of psychological and physiological events as factors shaping [consumer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer) economic behavior.

Psychophysiology is a monthly [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [scientific journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_journal) published by [Wiley-Blackwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley-Blackwell) on behalf of the [Society for Psychophysiological Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Society_for_Psychophysiological_Research).
Pulmocutaneous circulation is part of the [amphibian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibian) [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).
pulmonary circulation is a division of the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system) in all vertebrates.

Pulmonary stretch receptors are [mechanoreceptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanoreceptors) found in the [lungs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_lung).

Pulmonary surfactant is a surface-active complex of [phospholipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phospholipid)s and [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s formed by [type II alveolar cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_II_cells).

pulse is the rhythmic expansion and contraction of an [artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) in response to the [cardiac cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_cycle) (heartbeat).

Pulse pressure is the difference between [systolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systole) and [diastolic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diastole) [blood pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_pressure).

pupa (; : pupae) is the [life stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_life_cycle) of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s from the [Holometabola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holometabola) [clade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clade) undergoing [metamorphosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphosis) between immature and mature stages.
Pyrophytes are [plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plants) which have adapted to tolerate [fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire).

Radioiodinated serum albumin, abbreviated RISA, is a marker used in identifying [blood plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_plasma) via the dilution method in [renal physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology).

Radionuclide angiography is an area of [nuclear medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_medicine) which specialises in imaging to show the [functionality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Functional_imaging) of the right and left [ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart), thus allowing informed diagnostic intervention in [heart failure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_failure).

reabsorption, more specifically tubular reabsorption, is the process by which the [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron) recovers water and solutes from the [tubular fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubular_fluid) (pre-urine) and returns them to the [circulating blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).

Reentry is a [neural structuring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_neural_network) of the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain), which is characterized by the ongoing bidirectional exchange of signals along reciprocal axonal fibers linking two or more brain areas.

Reflexogenous (reflexogenic) zone (or the receptive field of a reflex) is the area of the body stimulation of which causes a definite [unconditioned reflex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unconditioned_response).

Refractoriness is the fundamental property of any object of [autowave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autowave) nature (especially [excitable medium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excitable_medium)) not responding to stimuli, if the object stays in the specific refractory state.
Relative Fat Mass (RFM) is a simple formula for the estimation of overweight or obesity in humans that requires only a calculation based on a ratio of height and waist measurements.
Relative growth rate (RGR) is growth rate relative to size - that is, a rate of growth per unit time, as a proportion of its size at that moment in time.

REM rebound is the lengthening and increasing frequency and depth of [rapid eye movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_eye_movement_sleep) (REM) sleep which occurs after periods of [sleep deprivation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep_deprivation).

renal chloride reabsorption refers to the process by which the [kidneys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidneys), having filtered out [waste products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_waste) from the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) to be [excreted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excreted) as [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine), re-absorb [chloride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloride) ions () from the waste.

Renal glucose reabsorption is the part of [kidney (renal) physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology) that deals with the retrieval of filtered [glucose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glucose), preventing it from disappearing from the body through the urine.

Renal oligopeptide reabsorption is the part of [renal physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_physiology) that deals with the retrieval of filtered [oligopeptide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligopeptide)s, preventing them from disappearing from the body through the urine.

renal sodium reabsorption refers to the process by which the [kidneys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidneys), having filtered out [waste products](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolic_waste) from the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) to be [excreted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excreted) as [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine), re-absorb [sodium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodium) ions () from the waste.

Wilting is the loss of rigidity of non-woody parts of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

definition: Windkessel effect (German: Windkesseleffekt) is a term used in [medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine) to account for the shape of the [arterial blood pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arterial_blood_pressure) waveform in terms of the interaction between the [stroke volume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke_volume) and the [compliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compliance_(physiology)) of the aorta and large [elastic arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_artery) (Windkessel vessels) and the [resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_(physics)) of the smaller arteries and [arteriole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arteriole)s.

Wingate test (also known as the Wingate Anaerobic Test (WAnT)) is an [anaerobic exercise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaerobic_exercise) test, most often performed on a [stationary bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stationary_bicycle), that measures peak anaerobic power and anaerobic capacity.

Winter rest (from the [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language) term Winterruhe) is a state of reduced activity of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s and [warm-blooded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warm-blooded) [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s living in extratropical regions of the [world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth) during the more hostile environmental conditions of [winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter).

work loop technique is used in muscle physiology to evaluate the mechanical [work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Work_(physics)) and [power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_(physics)) output of [skeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_striated_muscle) or [cardiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle) muscle contractions via [in vitro muscle testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro_muscle_testing) of whole muscles, fiber bundles or single muscle fibers.

Work of breathing (WOB) is the energy expended to [inhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhale) and [exhale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhale) a [breathing gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breathing_gas).
Wound assessment is a component of [wound management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wound_care).
Xenia (also known as the xenia effect) in plants is the effect of pollen on seeds and fruit of the fertilized plant.

Xenotransfusion (from Greek 'strange, foreign'), a form of [xenotransplantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xenotransplantation), was initially defined as the [transfer of blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_transfusion) from one species into the [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s of another.

Xylem is one of the two types of transport [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s, the other being [phloem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phloem); both of these are part of the [vascular bundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_bundle).

definition: Young–Laplace equation () is an equation that describes the [capillary pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary_pressure) difference sustained across the interface between two [static fluids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fluid_statics), such as [water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water) and [air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air), due to the phenomenon of [surface tension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface_tension) or [wall tension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall_tension) acting against the curvature of the surface (although use of the latter is only applicable if assuming that the wall is very thin).

zeitgeber ( , ) is any external or environmental cue that entrains or synchronizes an organism's [biological rhythms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circadian_rhythm), usually naturally occurring and serving to entrain to the Earth's 24-hour light/dark and 12-month cycles.
